# Mtek documentation

<!-- Generated by tools/release-docs (docs/README.md). Do not edit by hand: change the sources it reads, then run `npm run generate -w @mtek/release-docs`. -->

Mtek is a typed language for describing a 3D scene: its entities, its state, the shaders of its materials and the resources they need. The compiler turns a project into JavaScript and WGSL that a small runtime draws with WebGPU. This is version 0.1 of the language (mtek 0.1.0-dev (language 0.1, runtime ABI 1)); the project is pre-alpha, and [Limitations](limitations.md) says what it does not do yet.

## A learning path

1. **[Getting started](getting-started.md).** Install the toolchain from source, run a program, break it on purpose, read the error and repair it.
2. **[Tutorial: catch the crates](tutorial.md).** Build one program in seven steps: a lit room, a cart, falling crates with physics, a score, a material of your own and a second file.
3. **[Making a game](making-games.md).** Scenes, saved scores, timers, a HUD, sound, sprites and an itch.io upload, starting from `mtek new --template game`.
4. **The concept pages**, below, in any order. Each one has the same parts: the rules, why they exist, worked examples, the common mistakes with the diagnostic code each one raises, and links.
5. **[Language reference](language-reference.md)** when you need the exact rule or a signature, and **[Limitations](limitations.md)** when something you expected is not there.

A language model that writes Mtek should be given the **[language guide](language-guide.md)**: one page with each rule and one correct pattern for it, small enough to read in one go, with the concept pages as the place to look for depth.

## Concepts

| Page | What it answers |
|---|---|
| [Values and types](concepts/values-and-types.md) | Which types exist, why `i32` and `f32` never mix, vectors, colours, quaternions, arrays, and the names you cannot use. |
| [Functions and effects](concepts/functions-and-effects.md) | `fn` against `cpu fn`, what runs on the GPU, and why a helper is rejected. |
| [State and bindings](concepts/state-and-bindings.md) | Where data lives, what `bind` may read and call, how to derive a value, who may write a field. |
| [Time and input](concepts/time-and-input.md) | `update` against `fixed_update`, the duration clamp, held keys against key events, the key names. |
| [Entities, references and spawning](concepts/entities-and-references.md) | What an `entity_ref` can do, how to model "no entity", how `spawn` and `destroy` behave. |
| [Prefabs and scenes](concepts/prefabs-and-scenes.md) | What may appear where, why a prefab is one entity, static and dynamic instances, cameras. |
| [Lighting, units and colour](concepts/lighting-and-units.md) | Lux and candela, the camera exposure scale, what it does to ambient light, sRGB and linear colour. |
| [Materials and shaders](concepts/materials-and-shaders.md) | The fragment stage, what it may read, the built-in materials, instances and their parameters. |
| [Textures, samplers and assets](concepts/textures-samplers-and-assets.md) | Declaring images and models, path rules, sampler presets and mip filters, what is CPU-only and what is GPU-only. |

| [Modules, projects and host inputs](concepts/modules-and-projects.md) | Imports and exports, `mtek.toml`, and how a web page sets values of the scene. |

## How the documentation is kept true

- This index, the tutorial, the concept pages and the language guide are written from templates in `tools/release-docs/templates`, and the lists of names, field tables, defaults and signatures in them are read from the compiler's registry when the pages are generated. They cannot drift from the compiler. The reference and the limitations page are generated from the specification, the registry and the compiler as well.
- Every Mtek code block of the concept pages, the tutorial and the language guide is compiled by a test (`npm run check:release`, `npm run test:unit`). A program must compile and be in the canonical layout of `mtek fmt`. A block that is wrong on purpose names the diagnostic it must produce, and the test fails if the compiler stops producing it. The steps of the tutorial are applied one after the other, and each result is compiled.
- The getting-started page is executed against the real tool by `cargo test -p mtek-cli`.
- Every link between pages, and every anchor, must resolve, and every diagnostic code that a page mentions must exist in the catalogue.

Decisions [0116](../spec/decisions/0116-documentation-structure-and-generated-pages.md), [0117](../spec/decisions/0117-documentation-code-blocks-are-compiled.md) and [0118](../spec/decisions/0118-compact-agent-guide.md) record how.
